newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat on low dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat on low dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed unmoved against the dollar on Tuesday, due to low demand for the dollar and the forex market being well supplied with the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 58.49 to the dollar.
"With hardly any demand for spot, banks were involved in money generating swaps to buy forward dollars," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Dealers said the spot market was flush with dollars, mainly due to over one month of net foreign inflows to Colombo's stock market.
They said banks were buying forward dollars in the expectation that the currency would rise.
"It was not exporters but speculators that bought forward dollars," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by two local cents, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.4768 and 59.6582.

One-month forward contracts were about 26 cents above the spot rate, while two and three-months fetched 52 cents and 78 cents above the sport rate, respectively, the Commercial Bank dealer said. "These forward dollar rates are reasonable, given the current money levels," he added.
Overnight call money closed at 9.5 percent, after opening at 10 percent, dealers said.
